name: Biodiversity Hotspots Agent
description: Discovers and ranks biodiversity hotspots within a region. Bins GBIF occurrence coordinates onto an equal-area grid, computes species richness corrected for sampling effort, clusters dense regions with DBSCAN using a haversine metric, and returns ranked hotspots with a richness heatmap.
framework: none - a deterministic pipeline, no agent framework and no LLM
workflow: question -> region + parameters -> GBIF -> clean -> grid -> indices -> effort correction -> DBSCAN -> rank -> map -> AgentResult
managed_services: GBIF Occurrence Search API (count probe and paged retrieval)
knowledge_domain: Biodiversity - species richness, spatial clustering and conservation prioritisation
capabilities: Read a free-text question into study area, species and analysis parameters
Resolve a region name to a query geometry
Resolve a species name to a GBIF key, or ask for the scientific name
Estimate the record volume of a region before retrieving it
Bin coordinates onto an equal-area grid
Compute species richness, Shannon, Simpson and Chao1 per cell
Correct richness for sampling effort and report how
Discover hotspot clusters with DBSCAN using a haversine metric
Cluster one species' occurrences and rank them by record count
Tune eps and min_samples by an explicit silhouette scan
Rank clusters by the selected diversity index
Emit a graduated heatmap render specification
State the scope, the mode and the effort correction alongside every answer
cannot_do: Characterise the habitat of a hotspot (use the Habitat Visualization Agent)
Analyse temporal change or migration (use the Migration Analysis Agent)
Predict undiscovered hotspots - it measures what has been recorded
Claim that a low-richness cell is species-poor when its sampling effort is also low
Return a result without stating the taxonomic scope it applies to
Compute the IUCN threat-weighted index without a Red List token
Validate against the published CEPF hotspots without that shapefile
Render an image; it returns a render specification plus an HTML map path
Score a point it was not fitted on - DBSCAN is transductive, so no model is saved
Call a single species' occurrence cluster a biodiversity hotspot - with one species there is no richness to rank
confidence: High where sampling is dense, Medium where effort correction dominates

modes.region: biodiversity hotspots - grid, richness, effort correction, ranked by species count
modes.species: occurrence clusters for one species - ranked by record count, no effort correction
